title: Define storage schema for immutable Optimization Config versions + scoping (tenant/model/region)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
We need immutable, versioned “Optimization Config” objects to support safe apply + one-click rollback across Hosted/Dedicated (control-plane managed) and Private (version pinning + operator rollback). This ticket defines the persisted data model: how a config is identified, how versions are stored immutably, and how we represent scoping (tenant/model/region) without making rollouts/rollbacks ambiguous.

Goals
- Store Optimization Config versions as immutable records with metadata for traceability and diff.
- Support scoping by tenant/model/region (including wildcard/default semantics) in a way that is queryable and safe.
- Provide a stable identifier for “the config” plus monotonically increasing version numbers per config.
- Enable a pointer/activation mechanism ("active version") without mutating version records.
- Enable the safe-apply controller to atomically advance the active version for a given scope.

Non-goals
- Full rollout event history schema (tracked in ENG-4824 / apply controller).
- Audit log event payload storage (audit events emitted to audit pipeline; ENG-4826 covers event emission).

Proposed schema (Postgres)

1) optimization_config (stable identity)
- Purpose: stable logical config container; versions are attached to this.
- Table: optimization_config
  - id UUID PK
  - config_key TEXT NOT NULL (human-friendly identifier; used by Console)
  - created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  - created_by TEXT NOT NULL (actor; service or user)
  - deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL (soft delete; versions remain for audit)
- Constraints:
  - UNIQUE(config_key)

2) optimization_config_version (immutable version record)
- Purpose: immutable payload + metadata
- Table: optimization_config_version
  - id UUID PK (version_id)
  - optimization_config_id UUID NOT NULL FK -> optimization_config(id)
  - version INT NOT NULL (monotonic per optimization_config_id)
  - payload_json JSONB NOT NULL (full config payload used by runtime; schema validated elsewhere)
  - payload_schema_version INT NOT NULL (control-plane schema version)
  - payload_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL (hash for integrity + idempotency)
  - created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  - created_by TEXT NOT NULL (user id / service principal)
  - created_via TEXT NOT NULL ("console" | "api" | "migration" | "private-sync")
  - change_summary TEXT NULL (short operator-provided summary)
  - derived_from_version_id UUID NULL (lineage; helps diff/rollback UX)
  - validation_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' ("pending" | "valid" | "invalid")
  - validation_errors TEXT NULL (human readable, set by validator; versions still immutable after set—see note below)
- Constraints:
  - UNIQUE(optimization_config_id, version)
  - CHECK(version > 0)
  - CHECK(validation_status IN ('pending','valid','invalid'))
- Immutability note:
  - We treat payload_json and version identity fields as immutable. validation_status/errors are written once by the validator job. Enforced by:
    - app-layer guardrails (no update endpoints for versions)
    - DB trigger to prevent UPDATEs except setting validation_status/errors from pending -> {valid,invalid} within a short window (e.g., 30m) and only by the validator service role.

3) optimization_config_scope (defines activation target)
- Purpose: represent “where” a config applies; used for both apply and lookup
- Table: optimization_config_scope
  - id UUID PK
  - tenant_id UUID NULL (NULL means "all tenants" / platform default)
  - model_key TEXT NULL (e.g., "llama-3.1-70b-instruct"; NULL means all models)
  - region TEXT NULL (e.g., "us-east-1"; NULL means all regions)
  - deployment_mode TEXT NOT NULL ("hosted" | "dedicated" | "private")
  - created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  - created_by TEXT NOT NULL
- Constraints:
  - CHECK(deployment_mode IN ('hosted','dedicated','private'))
  - Uniqueness for canonical scopes:
    - UNIQUE(deployment_mode, COALESCE(tenant_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid), COALESCE(model_key, ''), COALESCE(region, ''))
- Semantics:
  - NULLs are wildcards. Resolution order for runtime lookup is:
    1) exact tenant + model + region
    2) tenant + model + NULL region
    3) tenant + NULL model + region
    4) tenant + NULL model + NULL region
    5) NULL tenant + model + region
    6) NULL tenant + model + NULL region
    7) NULL tenant + NULL model + region
    8) NULL tenant + NULL model + NULL region (platform default)
  - This gives deterministic fallback and supports “global defaults” without per-tenant duplication.

4) optimization_config_active (mutable pointer per scope)
- Purpose: points a scope to an active immutable version
- Table: optimization_config_active
  - optimization_config_scope_id UUID PK FK -> optimization_config_scope(id)
  - optimization_config_id UUID NOT NULL FK -> optimization_config(id)
  - active_version_id UUID NOT NULL FK -> optimization_config_version(id)
  - active_version INT NOT NULL (denormalized for fast reads; must match version record)
  - updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  - updated_by TEXT NOT NULL
  - update_reason TEXT NULL ("apply" | "promote" | "rollback" | "migration")
  - rollout_id UUID NULL (links to rollout controller state; introduced in ENG-4824)
- Constraints:
  - active_version_id must belong to optimization_config_id (enforced via app logic + optional trigger)
- Concurrency:
  - updates must be done with optimistic concurrency (WHERE active_version_id = :expected) to avoid apply/rollback races.

Indexes
- optimization_config_version:
  - (optimization_config_id, version DESC)
  - (payload_sha256)
  - (created_at DESC)
- optimization_config_active:
  - (optimization_config_id)
  - (active_version_id)
- optimization_config_scope:
  - (deployment_mode, tenant_id)
  - (deployment_mode, tenant_id, model_key)
  - (deployment_mode, tenant_id, region)
  - (deployment_mode, tenant_id, model_key, region)

Migration plan (existing optimization configs)
- Create one optimization_config row per existing config_key.
- Create optimization_config_scope rows for existing scoping rules.
- For each existing config payload, create optimization_config_version version=1, created_via='migration', created_by='control-plane-migrator'.
- Populate optimization_config_active pointers to version=1 for each scope.
- Rollout: ship DB migrations first, then deploy read path that can resolve both old + new until backfill completes (temporary dual-read).

API implications (for ENG-4825/ENG-4822)
- Version listing: SELECT versions by optimization_config_id ORDER BY version DESC.
- Active version resolution:
  - runtime/control-plane query uses optimization_config_scope resolution order above and returns the first matching optimization_config_active.
- Rollback: update optimization_config_active.active_version_id to a prior version id; does not mutate optimization_config_version.

Open questions
- Do we need environment separation (staging/prod) inside the same DB? Current plan: separate clusters; no explicit env column.
- model_key canonicalization: should we store model_id UUID vs model_key TEXT? Current recommendation: TEXT model_key to decouple from model catalog migrations; ensure a canonicalization layer in API.

Acceptance criteria
- DB migrations merged creating the four tables + indexes + constraints.
- Backfill script (or migration job) documented and validated in staging with >10k scopes and >100k version rows (performance sanity).
- Unit tests cover:
  - uniqueness constraints and version monotonicity
  - scope canonicalization and resolution order (golden tests)
  - optimistic concurrency update pattern for optimization_config_active
- Documentation: short schema overview added to the Optimization Config Service doc (Confluence) and referenced by ENG-4822.

Links
- Design: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimization-config-versioning-design.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-optimization-config-versioning-model.json
- Related work: ENG-4822 (diff + semantic validation), ENG-4824 (canary rollout controller), ENG-4825 (rollback endpoint), ENG-4826 (audit events)

Notes for Security/Compliance
- created_by / updated_by are required fields and must capture end-user identity when initiated via Console/API (not just service identity). Audit event pipeline is authoritative, but DB fields provide quick traceability in incident response.
- No payload secrets should be stored in payload_json (enforced by validator in ENG-4822; schema should not include credentials).

2025-10-10 Benji Okafor: Confirmed API use cases; asked for explicit resolution order for NULL wildcard scopes and an index plan for hot read path.

2025-10-14 Jordan Lee: Reviewed for promotion semantics; recommended keeping promotion/rollout state out of version table and using pointer table w/ optimistic concurrency to prevent apply/rollback races.

2025-10-18 Marcus Lin: Security review notes: ensure created_by/updated_by are mandatory; propose DB trigger to prevent mutation of payload fields; clarified that audit log is separate but DB fields aid investigations.
2025-11-01 Michael Nguyen: Implemented migrations + basic integrity constraints; added UPDATE trigger allowing validator-only transition for validation_status.
